messages:
Priya: Acme wants a concise onboarding note for Dedicated endpoint networking. They asked for options to lock down inbound and allow our callbacks. Need small bite-sized text they can paste to SOC.

Ethan: Recommend three patterns: (1) reserved static egress IPs, (2) customer forward proxy, (3) VPN/VPC peering.

Sam: I'll draft firewall snippets. Keep them minimal.

Sam: Option 1 - Reserved static EIPs
- Redwood assigns 1-2 IPv4 addresses for the POC pool.
- Customer allowlists these IPs for inbound webhook/callback ports.
- We commit not to rotate during the POC window.
Sample rule to paste:
```
ALLOW TCP 443 FROM 198.51.100.99/32
```

Sam: Option 2 - Customer forward proxy
- Customer provides hostname:port and credentials if any.
- Redwood routes outbound requests from the Dedicated pool through that proxy.
- Customer allows outbound from our pool to the proxy IP.
Sample rule:
```
ALLOW TCP 3128 FROM 198.51.100.0/24
```

Sam: Option 3 - VPN/VPC peering
- Private connectivity only, longer lead time. No public allowlist required.

Priya: Also confirm whether we can issue IP-scoped API keys.

Ethan: Not supported on hosted API. For Dedicated, network-level controls (EIPs) are the norm. Token-scoped keys would need an engineering change.

InfraBot: INFRA-9999 created: Reserve 2 EIPs for "acme-dedicated-poc". Owner: @Ethan. ETA: 48h.

Priya: Action items: Ethan follow up with IPs when allocated; Sam include a short curl test for webhook verification; I'll send the note to Acme.

Sam: Quick test to validate once IPs are live:
```
# we will POST from Dedicated pool to the customer test endpoint
curl -X POST https://acme.example.com/_redwood_ping -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"ping":"ok"}'
```

Priya: Thanks team. I'll loop Acme SOC and schedule a 15-min handoff if they want it. :+1:
